status: Draft codebook from the project proposal (section 5). To be piloted on Michigan and Texas and refined before scaling.

labelTypes.label: Direct quote
labelTypes.description: The speaker's exact words, from a cited source.

labelTypes.label: Reported fact
labelTypes.description: A factual claim reported by a cited source.

labelTypes.label: Source-based summary
labelTypes.description: A summary written by the project from cited sources.

labelTypes.label: Model-generated analysis
labelTypes.description: Analysis produced with an AI model; not a statement by the candidate.

labelTypes.label: Projection
labelTypes.description: A conditional, forward-looking estimate. Not a prediction or a fact.

labelTypes.label: Editorial judgment
labelTypes.description: A judgment by the project team, with criteria disclosed in the methodology.

confidenceLevels.label: High
confidenceLevels.description: Checked against a primary source; wording and date confirmed.

confidenceLevels.label: Medium
confidenceLevels.description: Checked against a reliable secondary source.

confidenceLevels.label: Low
confidenceLevels.description: Checked, but the source is weak or the context is incomplete.

confidenceLevels.label: Unverified draft
confidenceLevels.description: Not yet checked against any source. Hidden from the public view by default.

resultLabel.label: Election result
resultLabel.description: Vote shares and outcome of an election. Kept separate from the six statement labels: a result is a count reported by election authorities and news organizations, not a candidate's position.

resultStatuses.label: Unofficial
resultStatuses.description: Called by news organizations or reported from election-night counts. Figures can change until certified.

resultStatuses.label: Certified
resultStatuses.description: Certified by the state's canvassing authority. Cite the official canvass as the source.

policyQuestions.label: Federal preemption of state AI laws
policyQuestions.question: Should federal law override state AI laws?

options.label: Supports preemption
options.description: Federal rules should displace state AI laws.

options.label: Mixed / conditional
options.description: Some federal floor, some room for states, or conflicting signals.

options.label: Opposes preemption
options.description: States should keep the power to regulate AI.

policyQuestions.label: AI data center buildout
policyQuestions.question: How fast should AI data centers be built, and on what terms?

options.label: Accelerate buildout
options.description: Faster permitting; opposition treated as a threat to competitiveness.

options.label: Build with binding conditions
options.description: New data centers allowed if conditions on costs, local say, water, security or jobs are met.

options.label: Pause / moratorium
options.description: Halt new data centers until rules are in place.

policyQuestions.label: AI chip sales to China
policyQuestions.question: Should advanced AI chips be sold to China?

options.label: Allow licensed sales
options.description: Permit sales, for example under licences or a revenue share.

options.label: Restrict sales
options.description: Tighten export controls on advanced chips.

policyQuestions.label: Binding rules on AI developers
policyQuestions.question: How binding should rules on AI developers be?

options.label: Targeted binding rules
options.description: Specific prohibitions, disclosure duties or enforcement against specific harms.

options.label: Broad binding guardrails
options.description: Testing, audits, liability or licensing across AI developers.

options.label: Freeze or public control
options.description: Freeze powerful AI development or place AI under public ownership or control.

policyQuestions.label: Child safety and deepfakes
policyQuestions.question: Should there be rules against harmful AI content such as sexual deepfakes, harms to children and election deepfakes?

options.label: Supports rules
options.description: Backs legal limits or enforcement against harmful AI content.

policyQuestions.label: Workers and AI
policyQuestions.question: How should workers be protected from AI disruption?

options.label: Retraining and market adjustment
options.description: Upskilling and retraining; no new worker protections.

options.label: Active worker protections
options.description: Job or union standards, surveillance limits, or sharing AI gains with workers.

tracks.label: What is proposed
tracks.description: Concrete proposals (bills, moratoriums, plans) and official actions or votes.

domains.label: Data centers
domains.description: Records coded with the issue area "Energy and data centers", or with a stance on data center buildout.

domains.label: Everything else in AI
domains.description: All other AI policy: rules on AI developers, federal preemption, chips and China, child safety and deepfakes, workers.
